messages:
Alex M: Heads up — customer 'HelixBank' asked for an egress-control diagram for Private deployment. They're insisting on a 'circuit breaker' for outbound to avoid blast radius if model inference floods external providers.
Sam (AE): Timeline: POC next week, need checklist for netsec and pricing impact. Are we OK with PrivateLink + egress proxy? :thinking: 
Jamie R: Short answer: yes. We usually recommend interface endpoints for control-plane traffic, and an SNI-preserving egress proxy for model calls to hosted variants. For private-deploy, we support NAT + egress proxy in customer's DMZ or our managed proxy in a dedicated subnet.
Priya K: NetOps wants explicit circuit-breaker rules — rate limits + per-customer token quotas at LB. Can we suggest a firewall ACL sample?
Alex M: Quick snippet they can paste to firewall team. ```
# Allowed egress to Redwood control plane
# Allow outbound TLS to control plane (managed control plane endpoints)
ALLOW TCP 443 10.0.0.0/8 -> control.redwood-inference.com
# Allow outbound TLS to managed egress proxy (if using Redwood proxy)
ALLOW TCP 443 10.0.0.0/8 -> proxy-managed.redwood-inference.internal:443
# DNS
ALLOW UDP 53 10.0.0.0/8 -> 10.2.1.2
```
Sam (AE): Also need pricing note — will circuit-breaker/use of managed proxy increase bandwidth costs? Customer asked about per-GB vs per-request.
Jamie R: Proxy adds minimal bandwidth markup; main cost is egress to public internet if they route through us. For Private (on-prem/VPC) we charge a platform fee + optional managed-proxy data fee. I'll add precise numbers in the quote.
SRE Oncall: Operational recommendation: rate-limit tiers — 5 RPS per client token for early canary, burstable to 50 RPS with token-bucket. Fallback behaviors: 1) return 429, 2) queue small bursts for up to 5s, 3) flip to read-only model variant if sustained errors.
netops-bot: HA checklist: deploy proxies in two AZ subnets, place behind NLB with cross-AZ healthchecks. Healthcheck path: GET /hc returns 200. Use connection draining 30s. :white_check_mark:
Priya K: Perfect. Can someone produce a 1-pager for the security questionnaire (network section) we can hand to their InfoSec? They specifically asked about egress controls, break-glass escalation, and audit logs.
Alex M: I'll draft the network answers now and drop them here by EOD. Example entries I'll include: (1) egress allowed hosts and ports; (2) circuit-breaker thresholds and backoff strategy; (3) audit log retention and SIEM integration endpoints.
Sam (AE): Thanks — the customer also wants a diagram (simple arrow chart) showing: customer app -> private subnet -> egress proxy (managed or customer) -> optional internet/model-host. If we can attach that to the 1-pager it'd be ideal.
Jamie R: I can sktech the diagram and export PNG. Will attach after Alex's text.
Alex M: Draft will include this short FAQ snippet for InfoSec: "Can you block all outbound except our control plane and proxy?" Answer: "Yes — allowlist only the control plane hostnames and the managed-proxy IPs; DNS resolution can be locked down; for peered deployments we recommend VPC endpoints for control-plane traffic to avoid public egress."
Sam (AE): Great. Lean on the managed-proxy option for POC to simplify their firewall work. Priya — can you validate the ACL snippet with NetOps?
Priya K: Will validate and return with any port/IP updates in ~2 hours.
